title: Daily routine assistant
summary: The phone app I built and use every shift as Assistant Lead at a food production site.

story.heading: Why I built it
story.text: Mornings used to run on paper sheets, mental maths and WhatsApp messages typed from scratch. I built it on my own initiative to save time and reduce errors.

story.heading: What it does
items: Daily and weekly task checklist, with tasks that can be delegated.
Batch traceability in Julian date format, with checks on impossible dates.
Guided shift handover report, ready to paste in the team chat.
Daily stock count that flags products near their reorder point.
Packing picklists, pallet lists and the weekly roster, available offline.

story.heading: How it's built
story.text: A single HTML file with no backend, encrypted and hosted on GitHub Pages. Data stays on the phone.

title: Kanboard Web Page
summary: The Kanban board I built and use to organise my own day-to-day tasks.

story.heading: Why I built it
story.text: I wanted a task board shaped around how I actually work, so every feature exists because I needed it. I use it to organise my own tasks.

story.heading: What it does
items: Drag and drop tasks across To do, WIP, On hold and Done; every move is saved in PostgreSQL.
Priorities set real deadlines (High 2 days, Medium 7, Low 14) and overdue cards turn red.
Columns are sorted by urgency, so high-priority work is always on top.
Private boards per user, protected with Django authentication.

story.heading: How it's built
story.text: Server-rendered Django with Tailwind CSS and SortableJS, deployed on Render with a PostgreSQL database on Neon.

title: Ragusa Ecommerce
summary: An online shop for Argentine classics (yerba mate, alfajores, dulce de leche) with a real Stripe checkout.

story.heading: The idea
story.text: Build the full path of an online shop end to end, from browsing the catalogue to paying, plus the admin side needed to run it.

story.heading: What it does
items: Session-based cart without an account, with totals calculated from database prices.
Saved products, search across name, description and category, and category browsing.
Payments through Stripe Checkout in euros (test mode).
Newsletter subscriptions with a welcome email sent through Brevo.
Catalogue, prices and product images managed from the Django admin.

story.heading: How it's built
story.text: Server-rendered Django with Tailwind CSS, deployed on Render, PostgreSQL on Neon and product images on Cloudinary.

title: Ireland Rental Analysis
tags: Power BI, Power Query, Microsoft Excel
summary: How Irish rents evolved from 2012 to 2025, by county, property type and number of bedrooms.

story.heading: The questions
story.text: I defined two questions before touching the data: which property type increased in price the most, and which counties are the most affordable for family housing (3+ bedrooms) compared with Dublin.

story.heading: What I did
items: Took the official RTB Average Monthly Rent Report (RIQ02) published by the CSO, quarterly from 2012 to 2025.

Cleaned it in Power Query: kept the 26 counties, removed overlapping aggregate categories to avoid double counting, dropped combinations with no official data and split quarters into year and quarter.
Built DAX measures for average rent and growth that recalculate by property type, county or bedroom count depending on the visual.

story.heading: Key findings
items: Average monthly rent grew 124% nationally, from €612.59 (2012) to €1,370 (2025).
Semi-detached houses grew the most (+134%) and apartments the least (+112.87%).
Donegal is the most affordable county for family housing, and the absolute monthly gap with Dublin roughly doubled.
